subject: history_social
passage: In the 1860s, the first tea of each season to reach London from China sold for the highest prices, so fast sailing ships known as clippers raced one another across half the world. In the famous race of 1866, two clippers that had left China on the same day arrived in the River Thames within hours of each other after a voyage of ninety-nine days, a result so close that it was almost ______.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: Two ships that left on the same day "arrived ... within hours of each other" after ninety-nine days at sea. A finish that close is nearly a tie, so "a tie" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing about the result is unexplained; the text tells you exactly what happened.
explanation.B: Correct. After more than three months of racing, the two ships finished within hours of each other, which is almost a tie.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text does not say the voyage was the fastest ever; it says the two ships finished nearly together.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence is about how close the finish was, not about either ship losing.
